name: Garlic
description: Pungent bulb at the base of savory cooking everywhere.

nutrition.highlight: allicin only forms once it is crushed

guna.note: Excluded from sattvic cooking alongside onion, for the same reason.

effects.note: Meta-analyses pooling several hundred to close to a thousand participants across a dozen to twenty RCTs find garlic supplementation lowers systolic blood pressure, with the drop largest — 8 to 9 mmHg in the biggest of these — in people who are already hypertensive. Most of the underlying trials use standardized dried garlic powder at doses equivalent to roughly a clove a day, well inside normal cooking use. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.

Two independent placebo-controlled trials — one an allicin capsule, the other an aged garlic extract — found real drops in cold and flu frequency or severity, alongside measurable increases in the immune system's own natural killer and γδ-T cell activity. Both used garlic in a concentrated form, at a dose beyond a light seasoning but within reach of a garlic-heavy diet; a Cochrane review of the first trial alone called that single study's evidence insufficient, though the second trial's independent biomarker findings back the same mechanism. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
